description: This course gives fundamental concepts of the kinematics, dynamics and control of an industrial robotic manipulator.

syllabus.title: Introduction and Frame Transformations
syllabus.body: Definition, motivation, historical development, basic structure, classification, workspace, grippers, rigid motion and frame transformations, DH parameters.

syllabus.title: Kinematics
syllabus.body: Robot arm forward and inverse kinematics, redundancy resolution, velocity kinematics and the Jacobian, singular value decomposition, singularity and manipulability.

syllabus.title: Dynamics and Trajectory Generation
syllabus.body: Lagrange formulation of dynamics, trajectory generation - Cartesian scheme and joint space scheme, teaching methods - manual teaching and lead through teaching, sensors and actuators used in robotics.

syllabus.title: Control Schemes
syllabus.body: Position control, force control, hybrid position and force control, industry multi-DOF robotic manipulator case studies, design exercises in MATLAB/LabVIEW.

outcomes: Understand the basic concept of an industrial robotic manipulator.
Derive the direct and inverse kinematic equations of a given robot.
Derive the dynamic equations of an industrial robot.
Develop the control algorithm necessary to run a given robot.
textbooks: J. J. Craig, Introduction to Robotics: Mechanics and Control, Addison Wesley, 2001.
M. W. Spong and M. Vidyasagar, Robot Dynamics and Control, John Wiley and Sons, 2005.
L. Sciavicco and B. Siciliano, Modeling and Control of Robot Manipulators, McGraw Hill International Edition, 1998.
referenceBooks: A. J. Koivo, Fundamentals for Control of Robotic Manipulators, John Wiley Inc., New York, 2001.
T. Yoshikawa, Foundations of Robotics, PHI India.
